_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); railroad signals

pit_profile.why: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not

classification.quality_note: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 2.67x; +66% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.37; conservative 2yr -13%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -17.4%/yr (worst year FY04-FY13, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +11.3%/yr (Q2 2014 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +23.2%/yr (FY04-FY13 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +42.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY04-FY13); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: UNP (retrospective, 2014-07-25) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.67x (58.7% downside to Bear $42 / +22.0% upside to Bull $124) | Adj composite 2.69 vs market 3.06: gap -0.37 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +66% above the EPP floor $61 (13x FY14E $4.71) | Conservative 2-yr case: -13.2% total (-6.6%/yr) | At 21.6x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $134 sits above the BULL case; carloads +8% in Q2 2014, forward revenue +10% (no FY14 revenue guide, Q2 2014 freight revenue); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2013 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2009-2013 (diluted EPS 2009 $3.74, 2010 $5.53, 2011 $6.72, 2012 $8.27, 2013 $9.42; 2013 operating ratio 66.1%); 2013 diluted shares 465.8M, effective tax rate 37.7%, interest expense $526M, other income $128M, free cash flow $2,085M; 14,996,957 shares repurchased in 2013; competition (BNSF parallel routes); 2014 Outlook in words only (volume to exceed 2013 levels if industrial production grows about 3%, earnings to exceed 2013 earnings even with no volume growth, lower free cash flow); capital investments of about $3.9 billion
